A_target.statement:
Let $\triangle ABC$ be a [[Definition:Triangle (Geometry)|triangle]] and let the [[Definition:Angle Bisector|bisector]] of $\angle A$ meet $BC$ at $D$.
Then:
:$\dfrac {BD} {DC} = \dfrac {AB} {AC}$

B_source.statement:
The [[Definition:Area|area]] of a triangle with sides $x$, $y$ enclosing an angle $\theta$ is:
:$\dfrac 1 2 x y \sin \theta$

substitutions.the enclosed angle: half of angle A, shared by both sub-triangles

object_map.reformulation: Compute the ratio of the areas of ABD and ADC in two ways.

validity_conditions: Both sub-triangles have the same height from A, so their areas are proportional to BD and DC.
The bisector gives both sub-triangles the same angle at A.
proof_plan:
Triangles $ABD$ and $ADC$ have the same height from $A$ to $BC$, so:
:$\dfrac {\sqbrk {ABD} } {\sqbrk {ADC} } = \dfrac {BD} {DC}$

By the source result, with $\angle BAD = \angle DAC = \dfrac A 2$:
:$\sqbrk {ABD} = \dfrac 1 2 AB \cdot AD \sin \dfrac A 2, \quad \sqbrk {ADC} = \dfrac 1 2 AC \cdot AD \sin \dfrac A 2$

Equating the two expressions gives the [[Angle Bisector Theorem]].
{{qed}}
